title: Cutover orchestration index + dayhatch notes (2026-10)
content:
Purpose:
This is the operational index for the Oct 2026 midweek cutover. Not a final playbook — a compact working slate intended for the on-call/ops crew, release shepherd, and SREs running the watch.

Goals:
- Launch feature set: model routing variants + prefix-cache optimization behind feature flag V2.
- Maintain 99.9% availability during 24h ramp.
- Keep P95 latency delta to baseline < 15% for first 6 hours.

Quick summary (one-liner for pager):
- Rollout starts 2026-10-14 02:00 UTC, canary 5% → 20% over 3 hours if smoke OK. Fallback to stable model (v1) if error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m or latency > 2x baseline for 10m.

Preflight checklist (72–0h):
- [ ] Finalize canary config in traffic-orchestrator (ops-id: JIRA-2389). Marcus to push canary JSON by 2026-10-11 EOD.
- [ ] Lock deploy bundles (sha) and attach to release tag. GitHub PR #482 merged — verify checksums. Dmitri.
- [ ] Confirm dedicated capacity buffer: +15% headroom reserved in Dedicated pool eu-west-1. Infra ticket JIRA-2412.
- [ ] KV cache snapshot retention: ensure last-good snapshot is available (s3://redwood-cache-snaps/2026-10-13). Priya to confirm.
- [ ] Run smoke test harness against staging canary image (short run, 1000 requests). Results in /tmp/launch-smoke-2026-10.log. Sofia.
- [ ] Create temporary metric dashboards and alert routes: latency-p95, error-rate, qps-per-model, routing-fallthroughs. Use tag release:oct-2026.
- [ ] Communication: pre-announce to #release-notifications and stakeholders at T-24h.

Dayhatch timeline (day-of operations index):
- T-180m (T-3h): Final go/no-go sync. Attendees: release lead (Lena), infra on-call (Marcus), SRE (Sofia), PM (optional). Quick green/red checklist.
- T-60m: Apply canary traffic policy (5%), keep rollout paused. Run quick smoke (50 queries) and health checks.
- T-45m: Validate telemetry streams, ensure sampling and retention endpoints accept payloads.
- T-30m: Notify watchers in #watch-launch (ping shift roster).
- T-10m: Set propagation TTLs, disable automated scale-down for Dedicated.
- T+0m: Open canary gate -> route 5% traffic. Start 5m rolling window monitoring.
- T+15m: If health OK (criteria below) increase to 10%.
- T+45m: Increase to 20% (end of canary ramp). Hold and observe until T+180m.
- T+180m: Decision checkpoint (dayhatch): full ramp, hold, or rollback. Use the decision rubric.

Health criteria (automatic checks + ops verification):
- Error rate: rolling 5m error-rate < 0.5% and trending flat or down.
- Latency: P95 < 1.15x baseline OR absolute p95 < 450ms.
- Resource signals: GPU mem < 80% and CPU < 70% cluster-wide for model shards.
- Routing anomalies: fallthroughs < 0.1% and no sudden spike in cache-miss ratio > 2x baseline.
- Optional manual check: two operator thumbs-up in #watch-launch.

Fallback / rollback matrix (fast decisions):
- Trigger A (errors): If error-rate > 0.5% for 5m -> immediate rollback to model v1.
- Trigger B (latency): p95 > 2x baseline for 10m OR sustained queue growth -> scale down routes and revert config.
- Trigger C (infrastructure): Dedicated pool node failures > 2 nodes in 10m -> hold and reduce traffic to 0%.
- Rollback steps (fast path):
  1) Run traffic-orchestrator revert command (ops/revert-canary --tag v1).
  2) Post revert: bump sampling of traces for 30m (+trace:release-oct-2026).
  3) Open incident in JIRA and notify exec-watchers.

Observability & runbook snippets (queries to keep handy):
- Error rate per model: service.errors.count{env:prod,release:oct-2026}.rollup(1m) / requests.count(1m)
- P95 latency: percentile(latency_ms,95){model:variantV2} by 5m
- KV cache miss ratio: cache.misses / cache.requests (1m)
- Routing fallthroughs: counter.routing.fallthroughs{route:smart}
(Operators: paste these into Grafana quick panels; saved panel IDs in linked_artifacts)

Smoke test checklist (what to run after each ramp step):
- Basic generation: 200 prompts, validate response shape + no 5xx.
- KV-regression: ensure cached prompt prefix returns identical logits within tolerance.
- Long-context: 20 requests at 4k tokens to validate memory usage.
- Embedding stream: 500 vectors sampled for correctness and latency.

Release notes draft (to be refined for external):
- Title: Progressive rollout for model routing + prefix-cache tuning (Oct 2026)
- Summary: Live rollout of model-routing improvements that reduce cold-start latencies and improve per-request unit cost for medium-length prompts. Starting as a canary and increasing to 100% over a monitored window.
- Notable changes: smart routing policy, prefix-KV cache heuristics, minor schema for telemetry tags.
- Impact: expected 8–12% token-cost reduction on cached workloads; transient P95 variance during warmup window.
- Rollback plan: immediate revert to previous model and routing policy in case of elevated errors.
- Contact: release@redwood.com (ops) and #release-notifications.

Open risks / outstanding questions (T-24h snapshot):
- Cache warmup could take longer for large user cohorts — how do we estimate warm time? (Action: Priya to run synthetic cohort sim by T-6h).
- Observability gap: tail-latency traces for specific user ids not included in current sampling. (Action: Sofia to push trace filter rule).
- Edge-case: Some legacy clients depend on exact token alignment; we need to validate no tokenization drift. (Action: Marcus / infra).

Post-mortem template (post-release if incident):
- Incident timeline (minute granularity)
- Root cause hypothesis and verification steps
- Mitigation and permanent fix plan + owners + ETA
- Impact metrics: requests affected, user-facing errors, cost delta
- Lessons learned and follow-ups (tracked in JIRA epics)

Annotated TODOs (short actionable list):
- [ ] Marcus: finalize canary JSON and post link in this doc. (JIRA-2389)
- [ ] Priya: confirm snapshot path & run cohort warmup sim.
- [ ] Sofia: publish temporary grafana panels and add trace rule.
- [ ] Dmitri: verify release tag checksums and preserve build artifacts.
- [ ] Lena: run T-180m go/no-go and own dayhatch decision.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep dayhatch brief: one-page decision, one metric per decision (avoid metric overload).
- If in doubt on a noisy signal, prefer hold & investigate vs rash rollback unless user impact is measurable.
- This doc is intentionally compact; expand into a full runbook only if we hit an incident.

Slack links / quick refs:
- #watch-launch (primary ops channel)
- #release-notifications (stakeholder feed)
- ops-runbook: confluence://release-orchestration/2026-10 (detailed artifacts)

Appendix (local artifacts):
- smoke logs: /var/tmp/launch-smoke-2026-10.log
- sample canary JSON: /repos/infra/canaries/oct-2026/canary-5pct.json

---
Revision history:
- 2026-10-05: initial sketch (Lena)
- 2026-10-09: added rollback matrix + telemetry checks (Sofia)
- 2026-10-12: updated capacity buffer numbers and finalized timeline (Marcus)

End of doc.
